categories.main_business_segments: Tempus AI operates three primary business segments: Genomics, Data and Services, and AI Applications. The Genomics segment provides next-generation sequencing (NGS) diagnostics and other molecular and anatomic pathology testing. The Data and Services segment licenses de-identified clinical, molecular, and imaging data and provides clinical trial matching and analytic tools to pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies. The AI Applications segment develops and deploys algorithmic diagnostics and clinical decision support tools, including software as a medical device.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Tempus leverages proprietary technology platforms that integrate artificial intelligence (including generative AI), cloud computing, and multimodal data ingestion (NGS, imaging, EHR, pathology, etc.). The company operates high-throughput diagnostic labs using advanced automation, robotics, and proprietary workflow software. Data is structured and harmonized using natural language processing, optical character recognition, and manual curation, then de-identified and used to train AI models for diagnostics and decision support.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Tempus serves healthcare providers (physicians, hospitals, academic medical centers), pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, and researchers. Key end markets include oncology (its largest segment), neuropsychiatry, cardiology, and infectious disease. Life sciences companies use Tempus data and services for drug discovery, development, and clinical trial support.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s primary operations and customer base are in the United States, with data connections to approximately 3,000 healthcare institutions and more than 50% of U.S. oncologists. Tempus is expanding internationally, notably through a joint venture in Japan (SB Tempus Corp.), and has begun building relationships and data assets in other regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: Tempus operates as a vertically integrated, downstream provider in the healthcare diagnostics and data analytics supply chain. It collects and processes patient samples, generates and analyzes data, and delivers diagnostic results and data-driven insights directly to providers and life sciences companies.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Tempus’ strategic priorities include expanding its AI-enabled Intelligent Diagnostics across disease areas, growing its multimodal dataset, and embedding AI throughout diagnostics and clinical decision support. R&D focuses on developing new algorithmic diagnostics, enhancing data integration, and expanding into new therapeutic areas and geographies. The company also invests in partnerships, acquisitions (e.g., Ambry Genetics, Arterys), and continuous improvement of its proprietary technology platform.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated through clinical diagnostic test sales (primarily reimbursed by insurance, government payers, or direct billing), data licensing and analytics subscriptions to life sciences companies, clinical trial matching services, and, to a lesser extent, AI Applications (software and algorithmic diagnostics). The company also monetizes de-identified data through multi-year licensing agreements and research collaborations.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors in genomics include Foundation Medicine (Roche), Caris Life Sciences, Guardant Health, Natera, NeoGenomics, Quest, and LabCorp. In data and services, competitors include Flatiron Health (Roche), IQVIA, ConcertAI, and CROs like ICON and Syneos. For AI Applications, competitors include Roche, Caris, Guardant, Illumina, Myriad Genetics, PathAI, PaigeAI, and HeartFlow. Tempus differentiates itself through its scale of multimodal data, integrated technology platform, and ability to deploy AI solutions at scale.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2024, Tempus had over 2,400 employees and an aggregate market value of approximately $5.4 billion. The company has experienced rapid growth, with clinical oncology sample volume rising from 31,000 in 2018 to 350,000 in 2024. However, Tempus remains unprofitable, reporting a net loss of $705.8 million in 2024 and an accumulated deficit of $2.2 billion, reflecting heavy investment in R&D, data acquisition, and expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Tempus emphasizes its ability to deliver Intelligent Diagnostics by integrating AI with one of the world’s largest multimodal clinical and molecular datasets, providing personalized, context-rich diagnostic insights. Its platform connects laboratory results with patient-specific clinical data, enabling more accurate, tailored, and actionable recommendations for therapy selection and clinical trial matching. The company’s closed-loop, bi-directional provider network, proprietary software, and continuous data-driven learning create network effects and a competitive moat.
